- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next period; if below, increase by 5–10%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage trend reversal; adjust downward 1–2% if sentiment turns negative after peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle midpoint; align forecast to sentiment midpoint rather than peak.
